quote: I think we could, you know, get you to nine at least see what it look like.
stewart_read: The rep quotes a specific panel count to a customer who hasn't even provided a bill yet, guessing at design output the design team should generate. This is premature closer-tier content used to save a tree objection.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep may have been improvising to keep the customer engaged after a defensive statement, not intending to make a design commitment.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the universal escape hatch — acknowledge the tree concern and defer exact panel counts to the design team after the bill/usage is collected.

quote: I do want you to know I have trees, and I'm not cutting any of my trees down. Because the last guy that came out said I'd have to cut down two or two or three of my trees, and I told him forget it.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a prior competitor visit and a specific reason for rejecting it. The rep never asks which company or when this happened, losing competitive intel that would help the closer differentiate.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: rep may have judged the tree issue as more urgent to resolve than the company name, prioritizing keeping the lead alive over data-gathering.
coaching_implication: Prompt the rep to ask 'which company was that?' in under 10 seconds — free competitive intel with no cost to call flow.

quote: Okay. Wow. Yeah. Definitely. You know, it's more expensive. I know they've I've heard a lot of them kinda raising their rates and getting more expensive. So definitely see what we can do to help you cut that back there.
stewart_read: The customer just handed over a real bill figure ($331) and the rep responded with generic utility-rate commentary instead of flipping it into a reason to act now ('that $331 is what you're not interested in keeping paying').
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read only — there is no evidence the rep intended to circle back to this number later in the call.
coaching_implication: Drill the bill-flip language: acknowledge the number, then tie it directly to urgency/savings framing before moving to the next verify item.

quote: I do want you to know I have trees, and I'm not cutting any of my trees down.
stewart_read: Buried inside a defensive statement is useful signal: the customer is engaged enough with solar to have already had a design conversation with a competitor and is still shopping (see 01:08). This is a warmer lead than the guarded tone suggests.
coaching_implication: Manager should note this lead has real prior engagement with a competitor — worth flagging to the closer as competitive urgency, not just cold curiosity.

quote: My wife's my wife's got MS, and I'm in and out. My wife is up and down, and it all depends on her. So when you make appointment to come out, it all depends on what I have to do with her more than your appointment. I don't mean to be disrespectful, but
stewart_read: Customer discloses a significant caregiving/health constraint that shapes his entire availability, and the rep's response is a brief, generic reassurance before moving straight to scheduling logistics.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: the rep may have judged that dwelling on the disclosure risked prolonging a call the customer was already trying to end for a doctor's appointment.
coaching_implication: Coach a slightly fuller acknowledgment ('I'm sorry to hear that, take the time you need') before pivoting to logistics — costs 5 seconds, builds trust with a caregiver customer.

quote: Could you give me a callback in about an hour, hour and a half? And I'll have that information for you because I have to check my wife's calendar schedule.
stewart_read: The call ends on a callback promise with no locked day/time, no button-up recap, and no handshake confirmation — entirely customer-driven next step.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read: given the wife's medical appointment and caregiving unpredictability, deferring to a callback may be the correct procedural call rather than forcing a slot.
coaching_implication: Even within a deferred callback, the rep should have restated the specific time window and confirmed a fallback plan if the customer misses the callback.

quote: It was a a few hours more than I had last year this time, so I just kinda tossed it. So I don't have that available at this time.
stewart_read: Customer reveals his usage went up year-over-year — a strong forward-pulling hook (rising usage = rising bills = stronger solar case) — but the rep only follows up asking for the dollar figure, not reflecting the usage increase back as a reason to move quickly.
coaching_implication: Train the rep to reflect usage-increase comments back to the customer as a curiosity hook: 'that's exactly the kind of trend the design will quantify for you.'
